title: P65Pas 6502 compiler and IDE
reason: Simplified Pascal-to-6502 compiler with IDE/debugger and direct PRG output. Basic type/language subset only; inherited PIC-named identifiers do not establish a PIC target.

title: Slime Mori Mori compression analysis
reason: Implemented Huffman/displacement/LZ-style decoder modes for custom game compression. Narrow data-format reconstruction, not entire game code.

title: BBC Domesday Archimedes source archive
reason: Historical Logica A500 source is an Archimedes adaptation of BBC AIV, not simply the BBC release. Real BCPL lives under build/src/*.b; path rewriting restores build layout, and README notes RISC OS3 linking failure.

title: C02 6502 C-syntax compiler
reason: Expression/parser code produces DASM assembly for a deliberately modified C subset. Not a standards-complete C compiler; platform scripts may need path fixes.

title: Macintosh Portable ROM reconstruction
reason: ROM initialization source and power-manager material with ROMTools dependency and assembler optimization controls. Sparse documentation; partial reconstruction and build prerequisites must not imply independently verified complete ROM matching.

title: Taipan Apple II source analysis
reason: Despite TRS80 repository name, README explicitly says original TRS80 version is not yet present. Actual Apple II BASIC with keyboard PEEK/POKE and machine-code analysis plus mods; no TRS80 target claim.

title: Yie Ar Kung-Fu MSX disassembly
reason: Address-anchored notes, dispatch entries, generated listing and original-ROM checks. Easy/hard dumps compared separately; physical byte coverage and comment density are not identical semantic-certainty measures. Own ROM required.

title: Azure Dreams PSX modding research
reason: Shop patcher and separate unfinished second-town work with sector EDC/ECC repair. Modifies disc images; source was read only here. Finished shop features do not establish completion of town expansion or full decompilation.

title: Hopper X68000 executable loader
reason: Parses Human68k X-file headers and can mark DOS calls. Requires Hopper SDK and separate m68k CPU plugin; loader alone is not a standalone disassembler.

title: Macintosh resource Kaitai specifications
reason: Concrete WIND/BNDL/version/template format schemas with offsets and documentation. Core resource-fork/compression schemas moved to official Kaitai repo; this repository retains individual resource formats.

title: Pascal for Human Beings restoration
reason: Rekeyed1982 compiler translates a small Pascal subset into printed BBC BASIC, not native CPU code. No procedures,arrays,sets,file I/O or robust syntax checking; output capture required.

title: Magick2CPC graphics converter
reason: MagickWand conversion to z88dk/CPCRSlib sprite source with CPC palette/mode tables. Caller supplies correctly sized image, CPC Plus unsupported and CPCRSlib mode 0 is the tested path; empty README must not hide README.md.

title: mourix/MV-LED
reason: Concrete Neo Geo credit-counter PCB reproduction with Altium design, scans, BOM and Gerbers, but no firmware/software reconstruction. Retain as hardware-adjacent lead; current software target taxonomy does not represent board-only restoration without mislabelling it.

title: 65816disasm flow-analysis disassembler
reason: Script-controlled LoROM/HiROM analysis follows stack/register state and stops when immediate widths become indeterminate. Limited tested games and bank-boundary caveats; full-byte listing option can produce very large output, not imply complete semantic recovery.

title: KabutoCrunch C64 compressor
reason: C99 compressor and small 6502 decoders with separate proprietary and Dali-compatible bitstream modes. Credits Salvador, ZX0 and TSCrunch lineage; round-trip verification code is present but speed and compression claims were not benchmarked here.

title: PC-98 MAG image tools
reason: MAKI02 16-colour MAG decode/encode/palette tools extracted from ADV98 work. Requires width divisible by eight, excludes 256-colour MAG, and RGB quantization may alter colours. README explicitly discloses ChatGPT and Codex assistance.

title: IT to SN76489 VGM converter
reason: Converts specially authored Impulse Tracker modules through concrete IT parser and SN76489 mapping. Channel-priority and hardware limits apply; not an arbitrary sampled-module player or universally faithful audio conversion.

title: Phantom Fighter — Amiga source archive and modern recreation
reason: Creator-published recovery of substantial original 1988 Amiga game code plus concrete source-based native Python/JavaScript recreations. The modern paths implement game logic directly and do not use game-specific CPU pseudo-emulation.

title: Carnival — ColecoVision playable disassembly
reason: Primary documentation and source establish a distinct, in-scope retro-development project.

title: Handy Rogue — Atari Lynx roguelike conversion
reason: Native C roguelike for Atari Lynx compiled with llvm-mos. Based on Jakub Debski's Atari 8-bit BASIC 10-liner Roguelike, expanded into ten randomized dungeon levels with combat, pickups, scoring and replay. Makefile builds Lynx output and includes cartridge-packaging and Mednafen run targets; repository supplies .lnx files.

title: King's Valley II MSX2 disassembly
reason: Primary README establishes a WIP, fully source-backed and SHA-1-verified 128 KiB MSX2 disassembly.

title: MZF2WAV — Sharp MZ image-to-cassette audio converter
reason: Primary documentation establishes maintained Sharp MZ transfer and preservation tooling with source builds and multiple cassette encoding modes.

title: TrailBlazer — native BBC Micro conversion
reason: BBC Micro TrailBlazer written from scratch in 6502 assembly using the ZX Spectrum version as a guide. Includes fourteen levels, two modes, keyboard/joystick controls and saved high scores. README documents BeebAsm assembly and BeebEm disc creation; asm.bat builds the native game, menu and table modules.

title: Ultima III: Exodus NES disassembly
reason: Primary README documents sixteen disassembled NES banks, Ophis reassembly and MD5 comparison.

title: Batty — ZX Spectrum-derived native DOS port
reason: Ports CityAceE's documented Z80 Batty disassembly into native 386 protected-mode DOS C++. Upstream reports all 15 levels and all three modes playable plus pixel/frame parity gates. Those bounded parity checks do not establish a byte-identical original Spectrum binary. Reviewed on 2026-10-05; build/playability claims are upstream reports, not independent execution. Evidence: https://github.com/ddanila/batty-pc/blob/main/README.md https://github.com/ddanila/batty-pc/blob/main/Makefile https://github.com/ddanila/batty-pc/blob/main/src/physics.cpp

title: cas2uef — compact CAS to BBC tape-image conversion
reason: Narrow format converter; deliberately heuristic tape timing Python converter splits compact CAS carrier blocks and writes UEF 0.10 data/tone/gap records for BBC Model B tape recordings. Actual serialization uses UEF headers and chunks, with a dummy starting block for older BBC OS behavior. Requires compact nonpadded CAS preserving block boundaries, specifically the form produced by DumpListEditor; this is not a general MSX-game-to-BBC port. CAS has lost waveform timing, so generated UEF uses heuristic pauses/default timings and is not audio-archival quality. README only says output appears to work in BeebEm. The script overwrites the named destination file. MIT applies to the converter, not its input tapes.

title: Cat and Mouse — creator-remade ZX Spectrum Next maze game
reason: Steve Monks remade his own earlier Spectrum/Amiga/GBA concept in native Z80/Next assembly. Zeus project includes real maze/AI/object logic and emits .snx; README identifies tested Zeus 3.98 and explains compile/run workflow. No independent build/play; snapshot format and old Zeus expectations must be kept as documented. Earlier versions are provenance, not separate projects. README explicitly names tested Zeus command-line version 3.98, generated .snx and emulator/hardware run instructions; distributed snapshot exists. No independent build/play test.

title: CrabSCV — Super Cassette Vision demo and asset tools
reason: uPD7801 assembly Cart/Game.s initializes background/sprite VRAM and runs a VBlank-driven player update loop. Batch recipe assembles and pads a 32 KB cartridge image; host C++ sources convert PNG into SCV sprites/backgrounds. This supplies direct implementation evidence for a new Super Cassette Vision hardware label. Technical starter/example rather than a complete commercial-game recreation. Classified as tooling; native Super Cassette Vision development example and asset converters. Cart/mk.bat assembles and pads Crab.bin to a 32 KB cartridge; host C++ sources convert sprites/backgrounds. Fixed Windows paths and custom assembler dependency remain. The script’s success echo and MAME launch instructions are not build/runtime test results; flags remain unknown. Technical starter/example rather than a complete commercial-game recreation. Author offers own code/tools under MIT, CC0 or public domain; assembler, graphics and tool libraries have their own licenses. Graphics source README separately credits the supplied artwork.

title: dwimsy media-preservation toolkit
reason: Partial media-preservation toolkit; native PC-8001/PC-8801 tape path implemented, broad roadmap unimplemented. Pure-Python tape pulse/FSK/audio core, PC-88 T88 container/protocol implementation, convert/inspect/split/join and WAV/T88 filters. Actual dispatcher and PC-88 block/state parsing inspected. Broad disk/ROM/multimachine support is largely roadmap, not current capability. Amiga/C64/SC-3000 search matches largely come from broad roadmap/dependency discussion, not evidence of implemented support. Added NEC PC-8001 and NEC PC-8801 as genuinely distinct source machines: README explicitly documents both current streaming filters. Other machine claims remain roadmap. ChatGPT attribution in README belongs to the linked fat8_d88_tool dependency, not proof of dwimsy authorship. README documents an actual Dig Dug PC-8801 capture conversion and current PC-8001/PC-8801 streaming filters. This supports upstream runtime only. Run from checkout withPython 3.9+; no packaging manifest/installed command yet. Most other machine/disk/ROM support remains roadmap.

title: Galaga CPC — native Z80 arcade remake
reason: Native Z80 reimplementation of Galaga, using a CPC-specific overscan architecture. Actual enemies, bullets, stages, collisions, audio, high scores and capture/rescue behavior are implemented. No original arcade CPU execution or disassembly-derived port is established. Substantial native CPC clone with tractor-beam, stages and alternate-player logic; build and arcade parity unverified. Build.bat hard-codes G:\Amstrad\rasm_w64.exe and uses WSL/iDSK and Python. Cassette highscores are not persisted. No independent build, playback, gameplay-parity or real-hardware test. No top-level license detected. Galaga-related artwork/name/data provenance and redistribution rights remain unverified.

title: NONTAMA / MSX M-loader tape unpackers
reason: Implemented game-loader decoding with cartridge-builder support nontama_to_bload.py recognizes PC-6001 mkII NONTAMA headers, decodes loader payloads, and emits BLOAD data; mload_to_bload.py separately handles MSX Hudson/Honeybee loader tapes. mkrom.py generates native Z80 cartridge loader/trampoline bytes for the Warrior cartridge family using decoded data. README lists successful examples; implementation includes detailed analysis of an originally corrupted tape payload and charset smoke tests. PC-6001 mkII is a distinct hardware label that must be resolved before publication; do not relabel it PC-8001. Needs user-supplied P6/P6T or CAS images. MIT tool licensing does not license the games. Compatibility examples and cartridge-register fixes are upstream evidence only. A recent commit explains using port 0x7F for real hardware and PC6001VX compatibility; no cartridge/hardware validation was done.

title: Freedroid Classic — high-level remake of C64 Paradroid
reason: Original Freedroid Classic is a C implementation of the C64 Paradroid game with extensions, distinct from the later Freedroid RPG spinoff. Inspected main loop and takeover implementation contain direct game logic; current configure.ac requires SDL3, SDL3_image and SDL3_mixer and provides Unix and MinGW/Cygwin branches. Current source dependencies are SDL3, not assumptions from older SDL1/SDL2 releases. Additional JPEG/PNG/zlib dependencies are checked in configure.ac. Historical Android settings exist but were not treated as proof of current Android support. No build or gameplay test performed.

title: TTE Track Loaders — native Amiga floppy loading
reason: ttetrack.asm and tteturbo.asm implement CIA/custom-chip floppy DMA, MFM decoding, sector checks and retries. Turbo uses two MFM buffers so decompression can overlap disk DMA; both contain a 68000 ZX0 decompressor and credit Frank Wille loader lineage. Headers document drive-number selection as not implemented. External hardware include files such as hw.i/intbits.i/cia.i and a suitable assembler/integration harness are required; no standalone makefile is present. Embedded ZX0 code has a zlib-style grant, but no clear top-level license covering the entire loader suite was found. No PAL/NTSC, accelerator/cache or physical floppy behavior was independently verified.

title: virtnet.device — native AmigaOS 4 virtio network driver
reason: Native PowerPC SANA-II virtio-net-pci driver implementing legacy PCI transport, virtqueues, packet paths and Roadshow integration for AmigaOS 4.1. Source virtio.c implements I/O register access and device/queue setup; Makefile builds device.c plus virtio.c with ppc-amigaos-gcc. Upstream reports end-to-end TCP on QEMU sam460ex, approximately 24–25 Mbit/s with zero retransmissions in measured runs. Legacy/transitional virtio device supported; modern-only 0x1041 is not yet supported. Introductory multi-gigabit claims are generic aspirations; actual documented measurements are much lower and slower than the e1000 comparison. License says same as sibling virte1000 without a license file in this repository; licensing remains unresolved. Only QEMU testing is established upstream.

title: Pushover browser port (DOS-derived)
reason: Static and DOSBox analysis of Pushover DOS executables produced a browser game recreation using DOS data; promoted under DOS origin without asserting Amiga/ST binary or asset analysis.

title: commodore-64-more-disassembled-games
reason: This root is already represented by 8 title-specific catalogue project(s); root README and listing confirm the existing subjects. The extra agentusa.prg binary already has an exclusion decision.

title: prompt-or-die
reason: Claude Code productivity timer, not a retro-computing development/recovery tool.

title: seqbox
reason: General file-system-independent archive/recovery container; no historical computer software or platform-specific analysis in the project scope.

title: Bitmapper — C64 multicolor bitmap converter
reason: Concrete Java/Swing cross-development tool converts images to C64 multicolor data and exports Koala files, with palette selection, per-cell color constraints, dithering and a GUI. The nested NetBeans project is the repository's single tool.

title: c64_disassembly_reader — derivative hex-listing converter
reason: README identifies this as a converter of mist64/c64disasm's existing hex-assembly text into BASIC/KERNAL binary images. c64_read_dis.erl parses listed addresses/bytes, fills address gaps and writes bytes; it adds no independent disassembly, recovery analysis or substantive compiler. Excluded under the workflow's rule for merely converting somebody else's analysis; original listing attribution is preserved.

title: AmstradCPC6128 — ZX-Uno/ZX-Tres FPGA core
reason: Synthesizable CPC system implementation extends Miguel Angel Rodriguez Jodar's CPC464 design with 128 KB banking and SD-backed two-drive disk emulation. The repository includes machine integration RTL, Z80 core, disk-controller logic, project files and known-good board releases; this is a general CPC implementation, not game-specific emulation.

title: CPC Mastering tools
reason: Build/packaging collection includes already tracked iDSK plus 2CDT and gfx2crtc. Own dump-pal.py (MIT header) and BASIC loader are useful, but conservatively avoid separately counting this mostly vendored mastering bundle as new independent tooling.

title: SG1000 multicart (xrip)
reason: README explicitly says heavily based on already tracked aotta/SD-1000 and uses its PCB. Firmware/menu changes are real, but retain as derivative lineage rather than inflate independent project count.

title: Boulder Dash modern Amiga clone
reason: New Amiga clone with editor; no primary evidence of recovered code or historical file-format analysis.

title: The Air Dirt Demo
reason: README identifies full original assembler source for the group’s own 1996 Falcon demo, with no binary-to-source recovery claim.

title: amiga_reconstructed
reason: Three named Amiga intros/trainers from this collection are already catalogued. Remaining directories have not been individually matched to a specific binary or reviewed for distinct reconstruction code; defer only those unexamined components rather than the entire collection.
